You can paste this:

---

Hi, thanks for being open to this.

I built a small tool this weekend called Friction Fixer. It is for websites where people land, scroll a little, and leave.

Today, someone has to read the analytics, guess what is wrong, change the page, and wait to see if it helped. Most small teams never get around to that.

The tool does that loop:

1. It reads how visitors behaved. Right now it connects to PostHog.
2. An AI looks at those numbers and picks one small change to the page.
3. It edits the site’s code and opens a pull request.
4. After the change is live, it reads the numbers again.
5. If fewer people leave immediately, it keeps the change. If not, it undoes it.

“Fewer people leave” means the bounce rate has to drop by at least 5 points. Otherwise the change is reverted.

I would value a quick read on whether this way of measuring and changing a page makes sense, and what you would watch out for. Happy to share a link or jump on a short call if that is easier.

---

That is enough. If he asks for more, the next detail is that each run changes only one thing, so you can tell whether that change caused the new numbers.
